title: Mistake about the bargain’s basic assumptions
shortTitle: Mistake about the bargain’s basic assumptions
summary: Mistake concerns an erroneous belief about facts existing when the agreement is made. Relief depends on the significance of that assumption and who bears the risk that it is wrong.
notes:
Renner involved land and water conditions essential to the parties’ intended agricultural use. The court treated the mistaken basic assumption as grounds for rescission and then addressed restitution separately. Stees illustrates a different treatment of an undertaking to achieve a construction result despite unexpected difficulty.

Ask what fact was mistaken, whether the mistake was shared, whether it materially affected the exchange, and whether the contract or governing rule allocated the risk. A mistaken prediction about later profitability is not automatically the same as a mistake about an existing basic fact. The remedy also requires care: unwinding the exchange and compensating every expenditure are not identical.

textbookImport.basis: Plain-language synthesis of the cited casebook passages; subject to the jurisdictional and source limits stated there.

topics.mistake: Relief requires analysis of an existing erroneous assumption and its allocated risk.
topics.risk-allocation: A party may have undertaken the risk of uncertainty.
